userStories.title: Resolve sandbox loopback defaults and carry a session write exemption
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Resolve the shared sandbox loopback default and extend the policy session contract with one optional writable output.

**Motivation** — Workflow sessions get loopback closed under an allow-list, so with a global `allowedDomains` list, tests that start a local server or reach a local test database fail inside agent sessions and come back as false cannot-verify items.

**Approach** — Verbatim Design 3, nax-agent portion:
- nax-agent: a new `effectiveAllowLocalBinding(network: SandboxConfig["network"]): boolean` in `src/sandbox/network.ts` returns `network.allowLocalBinding` when it is a boolean, otherwise `network.allowedDomains !== undefined`.
- `buildSandboxPolicy` reads the flag through it. `sandboxBackendFor(config)` (`src/sandbox/registry.ts`) passes `{ ...config.network, allowLocalBinding: effectiveAllowLocalBinding(config.network) }` to `_sandboxRegistryDeps.createBackend`, so srt's process-wide `initialize` gets the same answer.
- `createSrtBackend` is unchanged: it still turns loopback on only for `allowLocalBinding === true`. That keeps `nax sandbox exec`, which builds its backend from a policy file whose network can only say `true` or nothing, from turning loopback on where the config said `false`. The policy type and srt's input still carry only `allowLocalBinding: true` or no key.

Verbatim Design 2, nax-agent portion:
- nax-agent: the `policy` arm of `SessionSandbox` gains `readonly writeExemption?: string` (absolute path). `sessionSandboxFrom(launcher, root, writeExemption?)` sets it, resolved against `root`, only on the `policy` arm and only when given.

**Scope** — In: network.ts, policy-builder.ts, registry.ts, session-sandbox.ts, SessionSandbox in types.ts, matching tests, and the schemas-sandbox.ts/types.ts default comments. The allowLocalBinding config comment becomes "absent: on when `allowedDomains` is set (see `effectiveAllowLocalBinding`), off otherwise"; the policy comment notes that the default is resolved before construction. Update the existing policy-builder allow-list expectation to include true, preserving every other policy field assertion. Existing registry singleton/probe-cache and two-argument session-sandbox cases are unchanged. Out: ACP edit enforcement (US-002), dispatch forwarding and nax docs/config description (US-003). `createSrtBackend` and sandbox-exec behavior are unchanged. `nax sandbox probe` gets no new warning about `allowLocalBinding`. `bot/review-run.ts` `reviewConfig` keeps its own `allowLocalBinding` default, which stays a superset of the new resolver (it also turns loopback on with an open network).

**Interface** — `effectiveAllowLocalBinding(network: SandboxConfig["network"]): boolean`; `sessionSandboxFrom(launcher, root, writeExemption?)`; target `SessionSandbox`: `{ kind: "policy"; policy: SandboxPolicy; writeExemption?: string } | { kind: "unavailable"; reason: string }`. Retain the existing asynchronous return and readonly members. `sandboxBackendFor(config)` target: `createBackend({ ...config.network, allowLocalBinding: effectiveAllowLocalBinding(config.network) })`.

userStories.title: Honor the single-file writable output in ACP edit permissions
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Let the ACP edit gate exempt exactly the session's writable output from denyWrite while retaining all other path protections.

**Motivation** — On ACP, `decideFull` (`nax-agent-acp/src/client/permissions.ts`) checks every edit target with `firstOutsidePolicy`, and `buildSandboxPolicy` denies the whole `.nax/features` entry, so Claude's `Write` of `report.md` is refused 5 times per story and the story review reports "TDD evidence absent".

**Approach** — Verbatim Design 2, ACP portion:
- nax-agent-acp: `PermissionContext` gains `readonly writeExemption?: string`. `routerFor` (`backend.ts`) copies `ctx.sandbox.writeExemption` into it whenever it sets `sandbox`. `decideFull` passes it as a new optional 4th argument of `firstOutsidePolicy`.
- `firstOutsidePolicy(targets, policy, cwd, writeExemption?)`: a target whose canonical path equals the canonical exemption path (exact, NFC, case-sensitive) skips the `denyWrite` check. The `..` rule and the `writeRoots` containment still apply to it. Every other target is checked exactly as today. The equality is on the NFC form; it is case-sensitive, so a differently cased spelling of the path is not exempt.

**Scope** — In: edit-targets.ts, PermissionContext/decideFull in permissions.ts, routerFor in backend.ts and tests in edit-targets.test.ts, permissions.test.ts and backend-codex.test.ts. Extend existing three-argument gate cases and existing backend cases without changing them. Use the in-memory fake agent's Claude branch through _acpBackendDeps.launch and enter the cross-package seam at acpBackend. Treat canonical, canonicalPolicyPath, hasDotDotSegment, withinRoot and withinDenied as existing primitives to reuse rather than redesign. Only copy an exemption when the existing preApproval-aware router actually sets sandbox. Preserve the existing unavailable-sandbox open refusal for Claude review/full; do not test that case as if it reached a permission request. Out: the session contract/default implementation (US-001), nax dispatch propagation (US-003) and shell sandbox grants. Forwarding an implementer's inline report to the story review when `report.md` is absent is not done. A Bash command writing the report path stays denied by the shell sandbox; only the agent's file-edit permission gate gets the exemption.

**Interface** — `firstOutsidePolicy(targets, policy, cwd, writeExemption?)`; PermissionContext gains `readonly writeExemption?: string`. The existing Promise<string | undefined> result and OUTSIDE_WRITE_ROOTS_REASON refusal remain unchanged.

userStories.title: Forward operation writable outputs into ACP sandbox data
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Forward the operation's existing writable-output option into SessionSandbox and document the shared loopback default.

**Motivation** — `buildRunDispatchOptions` forwards it as `codingToolFileOutput`, which only the native coding tools turn into `ownedWriteExemption`.

**Approach** — Verbatim Design 2, nax portion:
- nax: `resolveCodingToolSupport` passes `options.codingToolFileOutput` as the third argument of `sessionSandboxFrom`, so `acpSandbox.writeExemption` is the op's `fileOutput ?? writableOutput` path.

Verbatim Design 3, nax portion:
- nax: the `execution.sandbox.network.allowLocalBinding` entry in `FIELD_DESCRIPTIONS` is reworded (Integration), and `docs/guides/permissions.md` says loopback defaults on under an allow-list.

Integration target text: `Allow sandboxed commands to reach loopback ports. Defaults on when allowedDomains is set; set false to keep loopback closed`.

**Scope** — In: coding-tool-support-resolve.ts, its existing acp sandbox tests, config-descriptions.ts and root docs/guides/permissions.md. Read buildRunDispatchOptions and workflowImplementOp.writableOutput as existing integration producers: the former sets codingToolFileOutput from fileOutputPath ?? writableOutputPath and the latter returns input.reportPath; neither producer needs a behavior change. Enter the seam using the real options those producers build and an available fake sandbox backend. Preserve existing policy, disabled and reviewer cases. Out: shared sessionSandboxFrom implementation and network resolution (US-001), ACP permission enforcement (US-002). A Bash command writing the report path stays denied by the shell sandbox; only the agent's file-edit permission gate gets the exemption. Forwarding an implementer's inline report to the story review when `report.md` is absent is not done.

**Interface** — `sessionSandboxFrom(launcher, root, writeExemption?)` is called with `options.codingToolFileOutput` as its third argument. `SessionSandbox` policy data gains `writeExemption?: string`; no exemption is returned without an available policy.

userStories.title: Enforce per-story and feature-wide Modifies limits before planning
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Preserve up to 40 Modifies entries per story within a 200-entry spec bound and block silent overflow before planning.

**Motivation** — On a 69-entry cleanup feature, US-004 kept 3 of 17 entries and US-005 kept 0 of 30, so the deletion story had no authorisation to touch the tests it had to change.

**Approach** — Verbatim Design 1:
- `MAX_MODIFIED_FILES` becomes 200 and keeps its role as the guard over the whole spec. A new `MAX_MODIFIED_FILES_PER_STORY` is 40.
- `extractSpecModifiedFiles` extracts up to `MAX_MODIFIED_FILES` entries in document order, then keeps the first `MAX_MODIFIED_FILES_PER_STORY` entries of each story, also in document order. Stories are grouped by exact `storyId`, as `applyModifiedFiles` groups them; entries with `storyId: null` form one bucket of their own. Every extracted bullet counts toward the cap, duplicates of a path included.
- A new export, `findModifiesOverflow(specContent)`, extracts with no cap and returns `{ total: number; stories: ModifiesStoryOverflow[] }`. Each `ModifiesStoryOverflow` is `{ storyId: string | null; count: number; dropped: string[] }`, listed only for a story whose count is over `MAX_MODIFIED_FILES_PER_STORY`; `dropped` holds the paths after the 40th, in document order.
- `checkModifies` in `src/prd/spec-lint.ts` drops the `modifies-at-cap` warning; a new helper `checkModifiesCaps` (same file, keeping `checkModifies` under the complexity ratchet) adds two `error` findings:
  - `modifies-story-over-cap`, one per overflowing story: `<storyId> declares <count> Modifies entries; only the first 40 are kept. Dropped: <paths, comma separated>. Split the story.` For the `null` bucket, `<storyId>` reads `Unattributed entries`;
  - `modifies-over-cap`, when `total` is over 200: `<total> Modifies entries exceed the 200-entry cap for one spec; entries after the 200th are dropped. Split the feature.`
- Both codes join `BLOCKING_SPEC_LINT_CODES`, so `assertSpecLintClean` (`nax plan`) throws `PLAN_SPEC_LINT_FAILED` instead of planning a spec that would lose entries.

**Scope** — In: modifies-extract.ts, spec-lint.ts and prd/index.ts exports; extend modifies.test.ts, spec-lint.test.ts and spec-lint-gate.test.ts. Replace the existing MAX_MODIFIED_FILES+10-under-one-story expectation with the 40-per-story/200-per-spec invariant, and replace the old 25-entry modifies-at-cap warning expectation with a 41-entry error case. Preserve the shared markdown grammar and later applyModifiedFiles path deduplication; duplicate bullets count before that stage. Read applyModifiedFiles and assertSpecLintClean as existing consumers. Out: sandbox/report exemptions (US-001–US-003), other input fixes (US-005–US-009), planner-prompt folding and Context Files caps. The planner prompt's folding of dropped Modifies paths into `analysis` is not changed; the lint now blocks before planning instead. The `### Context Files` cap (`MAX_SPEC_CONTEXT_FILES`) is not changed.

**Interface** — `extractSpecModifiedFiles(specContent)`; `findModifiesOverflow(specContent)` returns `{ total: number; stories: ModifiesStoryOverflow[] }`; `ModifiesStoryOverflow` is `{ storyId: string | null; count: number; dropped: string[] }`. Export `MAX_MODIFIED_FILES_PER_STORY`, `findModifiesOverflow` and the `ModifiesStoryOverflow` type beside `extractSpecModifiedFiles, MAX_MODIFIED_FILES` from `@/prd`.

userStories.title: Parse bun check error blocks into typecheck findings
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Recognize bun check error blocks before other auto strategies and produce file/line/code findings instead of an opaque sentinel.

**Motivation** — `parseTypecheckOutput` tries `tscStrategy`, then `typecheckTextBlockStrategy`; neither reads `<error file="…" line="…" column="…" code="…">`, so `bun check` output parses to `null`.

**Approach** — Verbatim Design 4, parsing portion:
- A new strategy, `bunCheckStrategy` (`src/review/typecheck-parsing/strategies/bun-check.ts`, name `"bun-check"`), reads every `<error …>` block. The fixture below (`BUN_CHECK_SAMPLE`) is the output from #2662, verbatim; Bun 1.4.4 prints the same shape for a one-line error (verified locally).
  - A block opens at a line starting `<error ` and ends at the next line `</error>`; with no `</error>`, it ends before the next `<error ` line or at the end of the output.
  - Attributes may appear in any order; `file` and `line` are required, `column` and `code` optional. A block missing `file` or `line` is skipped. A leading `TS` is stripped from `code` (`"TS2769"` -> `"2769"`), the digits-only form `tscStrategy` stores, so `genericTypecheckDiagnosticToFinding` builds the rule `TS2769`.
  - `message` = the first non-empty line after the opening tag that does not start with `<` (so `<source>`, `</source>`, `<related …>` and `</error>` are never the message); text on the opening tag line after `>` is used first when present.
  - `raw` = the block's lines from the opening tag through `</error>` (or its end).
  - Under `"auto"` the first strategy with diagnostics wins, so output mixing `<error>` blocks and tsc lines yields only the `bun-check` diagnostics.
  - `<source>` and `<related>` children are never parsed as diagnostics, and `<warning …>` blocks are ignored.
  It returns `null` when no diagnostic is left.

```text
=== bun check -p tsconfig.test.json (exit 1) ===
<error file="test/unit/forge-tools/log-tool.test.ts" line="90" column="86" code="TS2769">
No overload matches this call.
  ...
<source>
90 |     expect(result.content.split("\n").filter(...)).toEqual(expected);
</source>
<related file=".../bun-types/test.d.ts" line="1030" column="5">The last overload is declared here.</related>
</error>

Found 1 error in 1 file, checked 3,668 files [602.81ms]
```

- `TypecheckParserFormat` gains `"bun-check"`. Under `"auto"` the order is `bunCheckStrategy`, `tscStrategy`, `typecheckTextBlockStrategy`. `toolForFormat("bun-check")` returns `"bun check"`.

**Scope** — In: new strategy and mirrored tests, types.ts and parse.ts, existing parser cases and a real-parser seam through typecheckCheckOp.execute. Keep explicit tsc/text/none selection as today. Out: sentinel output-tail construction (US-009), lint parsing and the other input fixes. No new explicit typecheck output-format value is added; `bunCheckStrategy` runs under `"auto"` only. `bun check` `<warning>` blocks are not turned into findings.

**Interface** — `bunCheckStrategy` implements existing `TypecheckParseStrategy` with name `"bun-check"`; `TypecheckParserFormat` target: `"tsc" | "text-block" | "bun-check"`; `toolForFormat("bun-check")` returns `"bun check"`. TypecheckOutputFormat is not extended.

userStories.description:
**Goal** — Surface inert package-scoping globs in rules lint without changing matching or failing the command.

**Motivation** — A glob such as `apps/api/src/**/*` never matches, so the rule is never delivered in that package, and `nax rules lint` passes it.

**Approach** — Verbatim Design 6:

- A rejecting `discoverWorkspacePackages` skips the check, as it does for `INERT_PATHS`.
- Only rules loaded from the root equal to the lint `workdir` are checked; `lintRulesForRoot` receives the package list as `[]` for a nested package rule root, so nested roots are not checked.

userStories.description:
**Goal** — Make package profiles feed runtime PackageView overlays and all existing override consumers consistently with workdir config loading.

**Motivation** — `loadConfigForWorkdir` applies the package profile, but `lintCheckOp` reads the runtime `PackageView`, so a package-profile lint command never runs and the gate records a pass.

**Approach** — Verbatim Design 7:
- A new module `src/config/package-profile.ts` exports `loadPackageProfileLayers({ profile, repoRoot, packageDir, logger, warnDedupe })`. It returns `{ chain: string[]; layers: Record<string, unknown>[] }`: the profile chain (`parseProfileList`, `"default"` and empty names dropped) and, per name, the profile data after `loadProfile`, `resolveProfileEnvVars`, `applyConfigCompatShims` and `warnQualityCommandChains`. That is the loop `loadConfigForWorkdir` runs today, moved.
- `resolveProfileEnvVars` is private to `loader.ts` today (it also serves the root profile layer). - Every `loadPackageOverride` caller now sees the package profile's values. Besides `hydrate`, that is `resolveGateCommands` (`src/finish/gates/quality.ts`, the `nax finish` per-package gate commands) and `resolveGroupCommand` (`src/cli/features-acceptance.ts`, a package's `acceptance.command`). This is intended: for the package-mergeable keys they now agree with `loadConfigForWorkdir`. userStories.description:
**Goal** — Make per-file and unreported-file coverage report-only under NAX_SANDBOXED=1 while retaining aggregate enforcement.

**Motivation** — About 60 tests skip inside the agent sandbox that run in CI, so `check-coverage.ts`'s per-file floors fail on files a story never touched, and every such story ends `DONE_WITH_CONCERNS`.

**Approach** — Verbatim Design 5:
- A new module `packages/repo-tooling/scripts/coverage-gate-mode.ts` exports:
  - `coverageGateMode(env)`: `"sandboxed"` when `env.NAX_SANDBOXED === "1"`, else `"enforce"`;
  - `coverageExitCode({ aggregateFailures, perFileOk, allFilesOk, mode })`: `1` when `aggregateFailures` is not empty; otherwise `1` in `"enforce"` mode when `perFileOk` or `allFilesOk` is false; otherwise `0`;
  - `SANDBOXED_COVERAGE_NOTE` = `[coverage] sandboxed run (NAX_SANDBOXED=1): per-file floors not enforced (CI enforces them)`.
  - `finishCoverage({ aggregateFailures, perFileOk, allFilesOk, env, log, error }): 0 | 1`, the tail of today's `main` after `checkPerFile` and `checkUnreported` ran: it computes the mode from `env`, prints `SANDBOXED_COVERAGE_NOTE` through `log` in `"sandboxed"` mode, prints today's `[coverage] FAIL — …` lines through `error` when `aggregateFailures` is not empty, prints `[coverage] OK — at or above floor.` through `log` when the result is `0` and every check passed, prints `[coverage] OK (sandboxed) — aggregate at or above floor; per-file results above are report-only.` through `log` when the result is `0` in `"sandboxed"` mode with a per-file or unreported-file failure, and returns `coverageExitCode(...)`.
- `check-coverage.ts` gains an exported `evaluateCoverageGate({ totals, perFile, unreported, env, log, error }): 0 | 1`, the tail of today's `main` from `aggregateFailures` on: it runs `aggregateFailures(totals)`, `checkPerFile(perFile, { list: false })` and `checkUnreported(unreported)` as today, then returns `finishCoverage(...)`. `main` ends with `process.exit(evaluateCoverageGate({ …, env: process.env, log: console.log, error: console.error }))`, so only argument reading, the test run and `process.exit` stay untested.
- The printed lines keep today's leading blank line: `finishCoverage` passes `log` and `error` a message that starts with `\n` exactly where today's `console.log` / `console.error` calls do; the ACs match on the message with its leading `\n` trimmed.
- The rule store says `test:coverage` is CI-only and must not be run inside a nax session; that wording lands by hand in the spec commit (Out of Scope).
